rules.title: No-Fault Evictions Under the RSO & JCO
rules.requirement: All tenant not-at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or the Just Cause Ordinance. Notices to terminate tenancy can only be served after filing the Declaration, and a copy must be filed with LAHD no later than 3 days after service.
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord wants to evict you for a no-fault reason under the Rent Stabilization or Just Cause Ordinance, they must file a declaration with the city and pay you relocation assistance.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su arrendador quiere desalojarlo por una razón sin culpa bajo la Ordenanza de Estabilización de Alquileres o la Ordenanza de Causa Justa, debe presentar una declaración ante la ciudad y pagarle asistencia para la reubicación.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to rental units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) in Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions_text: Exemptions include evicting a resident manager to replace with another resident manager, evictions due to hazardous conditions caused by natural disasters not caused by landlord negligence, and certain other conditions.
rules.quoted_span: All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with the LAHD makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO.

rules.title: No-Fault Reasons for Eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords may evict tenants for specific no-fault reasons including owner or family occupancy, demolition, compliance with government orders, HUD possession prior to sale, residential hotel conversion or demolition, conversion to affordable housing, and condominium or commercial conversion.
rules.summary_plain: Your landlord can only evict you without fault for specific reasons like moving in themselves or demolishing the building, as defined by city law.
rules.summary_plain_es: Su arrendador solo puede desalojarlo sin culpa por razones específicas como mudarse él mismo o demoler el edificio, según lo define la ley de la ciudad.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to rental units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance in Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: Not-At-Fault Reasons for Eviction 1. The landlord evicts for the occupancy of her/himself, spouse, grandchildren, children, parents or grandparents, or a resident manager (Los Angeles Municipal Code (LAMC) 151.09.A.8, 165.03.H.). ... 7. The landlord demolishes the property or converts the use of the property to condominiums, stock cooperatives, community apartment projects, hotels, and commercial uses, regardless of whether the property is subject to the RSO OR JCO (LAMC 47.06 & 47.07).

rules.title: Relocation Assistance Payment Amounts for No-Fault Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay relocation assistance to tenants displaced by no-fault evictions. The amount depends on tenant status (qualified or eligible), length of tenancy, income, and property type, with specific amounts set annually.
rules.key_value: $11,000 to $27,400 depending on tenant status and length of tenancy
rules.summary_plain: If you are evicted for a no-fault reason, your landlord must pay you relocation assistance based on your income, age, length of tenancy, and property type.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si lo desalojan por una razón sin culpa, su arrendador debe pagarle asistencia para la reubicación según sus ingresos, edad, duración del alquiler y tipo de propiedad.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants displaced by no-fault evictions under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance in Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions_text: Reduced relocation payments apply for 'Mom and Pop' properties under certain conditions and for single-family dwellings owned by natural persons under the JCO.

exemption_conditions.note: Mom and Pop properties with 4 or fewer units
Single-family dwellings owned by natural persons

rules.title: Relocation Assistance Payment Timing and Method
rules.requirement: Relocation assistance payments must be made within 15 days of service of the eviction notice. Landlords may pay via escrow accounts that cover actual relocation expenses, with payments from escrow made within 3 working days of tenant request.
rules.summary_plain: Your landlord must pay relocation assistance within 15 days after giving you an eviction notice, either directly or through an escrow account for your moving costs.
rules.summary_plain_es: Su arrendador debe pagar la asistencia para la reubicación dentro de los 15 días posteriores a la entrega del aviso de desalojo, ya sea directamente o mediante una cuenta de depósito en garantía para sus gastos de mudanza.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants displaced by no-fault evictions under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance in Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance requires timely relocation assistance payments as follows: 1. Payment shall be made available within fifteen (15) days of service of the written notice of eviction; however, 2. At the landlord's sole discretion and cost, the landlord may elect to pay the monetary relocation benefits through an escrow account.
